records.name: Alma
records.evidence_locations: Online catalogue, dictionary p51; competing origins and possible dates retained
records.facts_used: The catalogue attributed to Siliņš offers two explanations for Alma: Latin alma, meaning nourishing or kind, and a comparison with Amalia. These are alternatives; the entry does not establish one origin for every Latvian bearer. It places a possible Latvian written record in the second quarter of the nineteenth century and possible calendar inclusion in 1889. These qualified dates come from the online account of dictionary page 51, rather than an independently inspected original or a name-creation record.

records.name: Margiris
records.evidence_locations: Salys PDF116/printed101; PDF303/printed288 (1964 calendar)
records.facts_used: Antanas Salys describes Margiris as the form used by Vincas Krėvė in preference to Margis. He discusses possible compound reconstructions but stresses the difficulty of recovering the historical form; a proposed reconstruction is not a securely established literal meaning. The 1964 name calendar reprinted in Salys’s collected writings in 1983 lists Margiris with the short form Margys on 25 February. This documents a calendar recommendation, not the first bearer or the invention of the name.
records.uncertainties: Source scope and qualifications retained in every translation. Online catalogue claims are attributed, not independently inspected printed dictionary entries.

records.name: Tormi
records.evidence_locations: Rajandi PDF8/printed9; PDF158/printed160; PDF165/printed167
records.facts_used: Edgar Rajandi places Tormi among Estonian names formed from words for natural phenomena, here torm, storm. He explicitly warns that grouping it with Taima and Taimi saves space in the dictionary and does not make Tormi a derivative of those names. His 1966 book reports that one girl in Tallinn received the name Tormi in 1962. This is a dated local example, not a current population count, a first-ever attestation or a rule that the name can only be feminine.
